hypothesis: Surface EMG RMS amplitude monotonically tracks active muscle volume fraction a_eff during dynamic contractions.
result: Refuted in forward simulation: Subcutaneous adipose tissue variation (3 to 10 mm) creates a 40.9-fold uncertainty ridge, and fatigue causes an inverse dissociation (+14% RMS at -35% force) under simulated conditions.
impact: Eliminates scalar sEMG amplitude as a direct physiological anchor for active tissue volume.

hypothesis: Local muscle bioenergetic parameters can achieve empirical practical identifiability using existing disconnected literature datasets.
result: Refuted: When nuisance parameters (a_eff, h_fat, g_nirs, b_nirs, k_spec) are unfrozen, the system suffers a rank defect of 7, with flat profile likelihood ridges.
impact: Establishes that practical identifiability strictly requires simultaneous multi-modal recordings on the same subject.

hypothesis: Empirical cross-subject and cross-muscle validation of local bioenergetics model can be achieved without verified raw human time-series.
result: Refuted: Programmatic raw data acquisition from Dryad (Rehman 2024) and Figshare (Hug 2021) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Cross-subject LOSO on N=1 participant is methodologically invalid. Previous LOSO results were synthetic demonstrations. Status reclassified to SYNTHETIC_DEMONSTRATION_NOT_EMPIRICALLY_VALIDATED, and empirical validation is BLOCKED_PENDING_RAW_DATA.
impact: Prohibits labeling synthetic algorithmic demonstrations as empirical human validation.

hypothesis: Automated scripts can retrieve continuous open raw human 31P-MRS time-series from Dryad and raw HD-sEMG archives from Figshare.
result: Refuted: Programmatic downloads failed with HTTP 403 Forbidden due to AWS WAF interactive bot challenge on Dryad and Cloudflare R2 CDN protection on Figshare.
impact: Requires formal provenance gating and prevents synthetic data generation from masquerading as unretrieved raw empirical data.

hypothesis: Hug et al. 2021 reported Gastrocnemius Medialis discharge rates of 9.8, 12.6, 15.4, and 19.8 Hz across 8 independent human participants.
result: Refuted: Table 2 of Hug et al. 2021 preprint and journal publication reports GM mean discharge rates of 8.1, 8.1, 7.6, and 12.2 pps after manual editing. The eight operators were rater co-authors evaluating shared recordings from an unknown number of male participants across two reused experiments. N=8 raters != 8 subjects.
impact: Retracted unconfirmed discharge rates; replaced with published Table 2 numbers; classified biological sample size as UNKNOWN; barred equating operators with independent biological subjects.

hypothesis: More than 99% of energy in a 45-minute 250 W whole-body test is supplied oxidatively based on the ratio of single-muscle static PCr buffer to external mechanical work.
result: Refuted: Dividing single-muscle local PCr buffer capacity (0.62 kJ) by whole-body external mechanical work (675 kJ) commits a category error between static local capacity and dynamic whole-body flux, confounds mechanical work with gross metabolic expenditure (~3375 kJ), and ignores systemic anaerobic glycolysis (~75 kJ) and multi-muscle recruitment.
impact: Enforces multi-dimensional energetic accounting separating mechanical work, metabolic cost, ATP turnover, oxidative resynthesis, and glycolysis; bars invalid >99% oxidative claims for TARGET-CPE45.

hypothesis: Nominal exercise protocol timing (fitting from 90s nominal stop) reproduces true recovery kinetics, prospective prediction from t=90s is achievable without workload/perfusion data, model M2 validates multi-scale physiological balance, intracellular pH universally satisfies pH >= 6.86, and arbitrary MR signal amplitudes can identify absolute resting PCr concentration and active muscle volume.
result: Refuted across multiple dimensions: (1) Fitting from nominal 90s stop instead of actual biochemical nadir contaminates recovery with ongoing exercise depletion, underestimating k by 20-33% and degrading fit quality; (2) Prospective prediction (Scenario B) from t=90s prior to observing future nadir and post-exercise lag is blocked (PROSPECTIVE_PREDICTION_BLOCKED_UNOBSERVED_DEPLETION_DYNAMICS) because depletion depth and duration cannot be inferred without work rate or perfusion data; (3) Model M2 is mathematically a constrained monoexponential baseline model, not a validated multi-scale physiological ODE; full model M3 cannot be executed on relative MRS alone (M3_NOT_EXECUTABLE_ON_AVAILABLE_OBSERVATIONS); (4) Universal non-acidosis claim pH >= 6.86 is refuted by calculated minimum pH of 6.7932 in Trial 1 (range 6.7932-7.0228); (5) Arbitrary MR signal amplitudes are intrinsically scale-confounded with receiver coil sensitivity and cannot identify absolute mM concentration; (6) Single-coil MRS creates an exact unidentifiable scaling symmetry between active muscle volume and localized metabolic depletion; (7) Cross-subject LOSO validation is mathematically impossible on an N=1 cohort.
impact: Mandates empirical nadir detection for phase alignment; blocks prospective forward simulation without work rate/perfusion inputs; reclassifies M2 as constrained monoexponential; marks M3 as unexecutable on available data; retracts pH >= 6.86; maintains absolute PCr concentration and active volume as strictly unidentifiable; prohibits cross-subject generalization from single-participant MRS.

hypothesis: Successful multi-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out validation of macroscopic aerobic bioenergetic coupling (P_mech -> VO2) on cycle ergometry constitutes empirical validation of the full multi-scale physiological ODE (M3), identifies localized intracellular high-energy phosphate dynamics ([PCr], [Pi], [ATP], cytosolic pH), validates motor unit recruitment order, and validates extreme 45-minute survival (TARGET-CPE45).
result: Refuted: Whole-body pulmonary oxygen consumption and crank mechanical power represent volume-integrated macroscopic observables. By the many-to-one mapping (entanglement fallacy), an infinite manifold of localized muscle recruitment patterns, regional perfusion states, and intracellular phosphate depletion curves yield the identical systemic VO2 curve. Therefore, ACTES CPET data strictly cannot identify localized [PCr], [Pi], or pH dynamics (which remain bounded by Rehman 2024 N=1), cannot observe motor unit discharge rates (which remain bounded by Hug 2021), and cannot validate TARGET-CPE45, which requires a dedicated continuous 45-minute endurance test rather than a 15-minute incremental graded ramp to exhaustion.
impact: Prevents false claims of full physiological model validation. Strictly confines ACTES validation to macroscopic aerobic efficiency (eta_gross) and Phase II response kinetics (tau). Establishes REMAINING_BARRIERS_MATRIX and maintains TARGET-CPE45 as NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED and biological interventions as NO_GO.

hypothesis: Single-variable linear body mass scaling (P/M) universally improves prediction across all individual human subjects, and macroscopic cycling efficiency parameters (delta efficiency eta_delta, regression slope beta1) directly transfer to running locomotion without modality-specific calibration.
result: Refuted on two empirical grounds: (1) In the ACTES cycling cohort (EXP-0043), while linear mass normalization improves macro-average R2 across the full cohort, it worsens prediction RMSE in 7 of the 18 participants (Subjects 3, 4, 6, 15, 16, 17, 18), demonstrating that simple linear mass scaling introduces individual bias for light endurance and heavy muscular athletes; (2) In the Malaga treadmill cohort (EXP-0044, N=979 tests, 575,087 observations), naively transferring cycling delta efficiency (beta1 = 0.00766 L/min/W, eta_delta = 25.5%) to treadmill running incurs a severe performance penalty (RMSE increases by +179.1 mL/min, +44.3% error penalty; R2 drops from 0.6712 to 0.3727) due to elastic tendon energy storage/recoil and vertical center-of-mass oscillations present in running but absent in seated cycling.
impact: Prohibits universal application of uncalibrated linear body mass scaling without individual body composition accounting; bars direct cross-modality parameter transfer between cycling and running; mandates modality-specific locomotion models.
